custom_g_codes.description: Constant surface speed (CSS) mode. Controller adjusts RPM based on cutting diameter to maintain constant SFM.
Constant RPM mode. Spindle runs at fixed RPM regardless of cutting diameter.
Spindle speed clamp for CSS mode. Sets maximum RPM limit to prevent spindle overspeed at small diameters.
OD/ID rough turning cycle (Type I). Automatic multi-pass roughing parallel to Z-axis with depth of cut and retract.
custom_g_codes.syntax:
G71 U[depth] R[retract]
G71 P[start_n] Q[end_n] U[finish_X] W[finish_Z] F[feed]

custom_g_codes.description: Facing rough turning cycle. Multi-pass roughing parallel to X-axis for facing operations.
custom_g_codes.syntax:
G72 W[depth] R[retract]
G72 P[start_n] Q[end_n] U[finish_X] W[finish_Z] F[feed]

custom_g_codes.description: Pattern repeating (contour) rough turning cycle. Follows a profile shape with incremental infeed — ideal for castings and forgings with near-net shape.
custom_g_codes.syntax:
G73 U[relief_X] W[relief_Z] R[num_passes]
G73 P[start_n] Q[end_n] U[finish_X] W[finish_Z] F[feed]

custom_g_codes.description: Finish turning cycle. Follows the contour defined in G71/G72/G73 at finish feed and speed for final pass.
Peck drilling cycle on Z-axis. Deep hole drilling with full retract chip evacuation for center drilling and gun drilling.
custom_g_codes.syntax:
G74 R[retract]
G74 Z[depth] Q[peck_um] F[feed]

custom_g_codes.description: Grooving cycle on X-axis. Plunge grooving with peck and retract for OD, ID, and face grooves.
custom_g_codes.syntax:
G75 R[retract]
G75 X[diameter] Z[width_end] P[peck_um] Q[step_um] F[feed]

custom_g_codes.description: Multi-pass threading cycle. Automatic compound threading with configurable infeed angle, spring passes, and thread depth.
custom_g_codes.syntax:
G76 P[passes][spring][angle] Q[min_depth_um] R[finish_allow]
G76 X[minor_dia] Z[length] P[thread_depth_um] Q[first_cut_um] F[pitch]

custom_g_codes.description: Work coordinate offset setting from program. Sets WCS values programmatically.
Polar coordinate interpolation mode. Converts XC moves to polar coordinates for face milling patterns on C-axis equipped machines.
Cylindrical interpolation mode. Maps XC plane onto cylinder surface for engraving or milling features on round parts.
Machine zero return. Sends axis to home position via intermediate point for safe tool change clearance.
Single-pass constant-lead threading. Used for non-standard threads, multi-start threads, and thread repair.
Threading cycle (simple). Single-block threading cycle for each pass — gives operator maximum control over thread depth per pass.

custom_m_codes.description: Spindle forward (CCW when viewed from tailstock). Standard cutting direction for OD turning with standard insert orientation.
Spindle reverse (CW when viewed from tailstock). Used for reverse threading and certain boring operations.
Spindle stop. Decelerates spindle to zero RPM.
Coolant ON (flood). Activates main coolant pump.
Coolant OFF. Stops all coolant flow.
Chuck clamp. Activates hydraulic chuck to grip workpiece. Must confirm with M10 before cycle start.
Chuck unclamp. Releases hydraulic chuck jaws. Interlocked to prevent unclamp during spindle rotation.
Turret index forward. Commands turret to rotate CW to next station.
Turret index reverse. Commands turret to rotate CCW to previous station.
Tailstock advance. Extends tailstock quill to workpiece with preset pressure.
Tailstock retract. Retracts tailstock quill to home position.
Rigid tapping mode. Synchronizes live tool spindle RPM with Z-axis feed for tapping with C-axis.
Low gear select. Manually forces spindle to low gear range (35-800 RPM, max 530 Nm).
High gear select. Manually forces spindle to high gear range (800-4000 RPM, max 120 Nm).
Through-tool coolant ON (live tooling). Activates coolant through the live tool holder.
Through-tool coolant OFF.
Parts catcher advance. Extends pneumatic parts catcher into position.
Parts catcher retract. Retracts parts catcher and deposits part into conveyor.
Work counter increment. Adds 1 to the part count displayed on controller.
Program end and rewind / Subprogram return.
Air blow ON. Activates turret-face air blast for chip clearing during turning.
Air blow OFF.
Bar feeder feed command. Signals bar feeder to push bar stock to spindle stop.
Bar feeder retract command. Retracts bar feeder pusher finger.
Tool breakage detection cycle. Initiates tool probe check for detecting broken or worn tools.

probing_cycles.description: Skip cutting / probe touch signal. Moves axis until probe triggers, stores touched position in system variable.
Automatic tool setting. Measures tool X and Z offsets using tool setter arm with auto-compensation.
Tool nose radius measurement. Measures and stores tool nose radius for TNRC (Tool Nose Radius Compensation).

alarm_codes.description: Program format error. Illegal character or invalid syntax in NC program block.
probable_causes: Invalid G-code or M-code in program block
Missing decimal point in coordinate value
corrective_actions: Check the program line indicated in the alarm detail
Verify G/M code is valid for OSP-P300L
Remove illegal characters and re-transfer program

alarm_codes.description: Address command error. Required address letter missing or duplicated in block.
probable_causes: Feed rate F not specified for cutting move
corrective_actions: Add missing address value to the block
Remove duplicate addresses
Specify F word for G01/G02/G03 moves

alarm_codes.description: G-code group conflict. Two G-codes from the same modal group in one block.
probable_causes: G96 and G97 in the same block
G00 and G01 in the same block
Post processor outputting conflicting modal codes
corrective_actions: Split conflicting G-codes into separate blocks
Fix post processor modal group handling
Check manual for lathe G-code modal group assignments

alarm_codes.description: Travel limit exceeded in program. Commanded position exceeds soft limit for X or Z axis.
probable_causes: Programmed coordinate beyond X:260mm or Z:650mm travel range
Work offset + programmed position exceeds limit
G71/G72 roughing cycle generates path beyond travel
corrective_actions: Verify programmed coordinates against machine travel limits
Check and correct work offset values
Dry-run program with single block to find offending line

alarm_codes.description: Circular interpolation error. Arc endpoint does not match calculated arc from I/K or R values.
probable_causes: I/K values inconsistent with start and endpoint
Post processor CAM output rounding error
corrective_actions: Recalculate arc center (I/K) or radius (R)
Increase arc tolerance in CAM post processor
Split large arcs into smaller segments

alarm_codes.description: Spindle speed command error. S-value exceeds maximum RPM or G50 clamp not set in G96 mode.
probable_causes: G96 CSS active without G50 clamp — RPM unlimited at small diameters
corrective_actions: Reduce S value to within spindle range (35-4000)
Always set G50 S[max_rpm] before G96
Verify S word is present before cutting moves

alarm_codes.description: Macro variable out of range. Macro calculation result exceeds variable storage limits.
probable_causes: Division by zero in macro expression
corrective_actions: Check macro expression for division by zero
Add bounds checking in macro program
Initialize all variables before use

alarm_codes.description: Main power supply voltage abnormal. Input power voltage outside acceptable range.
probable_causes: Facility power supply voltage sag or spike
Loose connection on main power input terminal
corrective_actions: Check incoming power voltage at main disconnect (200-230V 3-phase)
Inspect and tighten all connections at main breaker
Contact electrician to verify facility power quality

alarm_codes.description: Battery voltage low. CNC memory backup battery approaching end of life.
probable_causes: Frequent power cycling accelerating battery drain
corrective_actions: Replace CMOS battery within 24 hours of alarm
Back up all programs and parameters before battery replacement
Replace battery with machine power ON to preserve memory

parts_needed.description: Lithium backup battery CR2032 holder assembly

alarm_codes.description: Spindle motor overheat. Spindle motor winding temperature exceeded thermal limit.
probable_causes: Sustained heavy cutting in low gear exceeding 80% torque
Spindle cooling unit malfunction or low oil level
Large diameter part in CSS mode forcing low RPM / high torque continuously
corrective_actions: Stop machine and allow spindle to cool for 30 minutes
Check spindle cooler oil level
Reduce cutting depth or switch to lighter roughing passes
Verify spindle cooling fan operation

alarm_codes.description: Spindle bearing temperature abnormal. Bearing thermocouple reading exceeded 65 deg C.
probable_causes: Bearing preload change due to thermal growth
Bearing damage from crash or workpiece shift in chuck
corrective_actions: Stop spindle immediately and allow cooldown
Check spindle oil level and condition
Run spindle warmup cycle after cooldown
If alarm recurs, bearing inspection required by Okuma service

alarm_codes.description: X-axis servo error excessive. Following error exceeded alarm threshold during motion.
probable_causes: Turret collision with workpiece or chuck
Ball screw or guideway binding from lack of lubrication
corrective_actions: Jog X-axis slowly to check for mechanical binding
Check way lube level and pump operation
Inspect X-axis ball screw for damage
Check encoder connections

alarm_codes.description: Z-axis servo error excessive. Following error exceeded alarm threshold.
probable_causes: Chip buildup jamming Z-axis way cover
Ball screw coupling loose or damaged
corrective_actions: Check for chip buildup around Z-axis way covers
Jog Z-axis slowly with low feed override
Inspect ball screw coupling for looseness
Verify servo motor brake releases when servo is enabled

alarm_codes.description: Hardware overtravel X+ axis. Physical limit switch triggered on X positive direction.
corrective_actions: Release overtravel by holding override button and jogging away from limit
Re-home the machine
Check that work offsets and program stay within X travel of 260mm

alarm_codes.description: Chuck pressure low. Hydraulic chuck clamping pressure below safe operating minimum.
corrective_actions: STOP MACHINE IMMEDIATELY - risk of workpiece ejection
Check hydraulic oil level in reservoir
Verify hydraulic pressure on gauge reads 25-40 bar
Inspect chuck cylinder seals for leaks
Do NOT run spindle until pressure is restored

alarm_codes.description: Chuck not clamped. Chuck open/close sensor indicates jaws are not fully clamped before cycle start.
probable_causes: Chuck not clamped after part load (M10 not executed)
Workpiece diameter too large for jaw stroke
Chuck proximity sensor out of adjustment
Jaw not seated in serrations correctly
corrective_actions: Execute M10 to clamp chuck
Verify workpiece diameter is within jaw gripping range
Adjust chuck proximity sensor gap (0.5-1.0mm)
Reseat jaws and verify serration engagement

alarm_codes.description: Tailstock position error. Tailstock quill did not reach commanded position within timeout.
probable_causes: Chip buildup preventing tailstock quill advance
Workpiece center hole missing or misaligned
corrective_actions: Clean chip buildup from tailstock area
Verify tailstock hydraulic pressure (20-35 bar)
Ensure workpiece has proper center drill hole
Check tailstock quill advance/retract sensors

alarm_codes.description: Tailstock not retracted. Tailstock quill not in home position during turret index or tool change.
probable_causes: M27 retract not programmed before turret index
corrective_actions: Add M27 before T-code tool change blocks
Check tailstock home position sensor alignment
Verify hydraulic pressure

alarm_codes.description: Turret index error. Turret failed to complete rotation to commanded station.
probable_causes: Tool extending beyond turret clearance envelope
corrective_actions: Clear chips from turret base and tool stations
Run turret home cycle from maintenance menu
Check that no tool protrudes beyond turret clearance radius
Inspect turret coupling teeth for damage

alarm_codes.description: Turret clamp error. Turret curvic coupling not fully engaged after index.
probable_causes: Curvic coupling contaminated with chips or coolant
Turret position sensor misalignment after crash
corrective_actions: Clean curvic coupling faces with solvent and brush
Verify turret clamp hydraulic pressure
Re-home turret and check station alignment
If persistent, curvic coupling inspection required

alarm_codes.description: Bar feeder communication error. Bar feeder controller not responding to CNC handshake signals.
corrective_actions: Verify bar feeder is powered on
Check communication cable between bar feeder and CNC
Restart bar feeder controller
Check interface relay board connections at CNC side

alarm_codes.description: Bar stock end detected. Bar feeder remnant pusher has reached minimum stock length.
probable_causes: Bar stock consumed — normal end of bar
corrective_actions: Load new bar stock into feeder channel
Part off remnant and eject
Adjust remnant detection length if material is being wasted

alarm_codes.description: Bar feeder push pressure abnormal. Bar stock not reaching spindle collet/chuck stop position.
probable_causes: Bar stock bent or out of round
Collet/chuck not fully open for bar feed
Guide channel misaligned to spindle bore
corrective_actions: Check bar stock straightness
Verify M11 chuck open before bar feed command
Align bar feeder guide channel with spindle bore
Check bar feeder hydraulic pressure

alarm_codes.description: Way lube oil level low. Centralized lubrication reservoir below minimum level.
probable_causes: Lubrication line leak at way cover or fitting
corrective_actions: Refill way lube reservoir with ISO VG68 lubricant
Inspect all lubrication lines and fittings for leaks
Verify pump operation by observing oil flow

alarm_codes.description: Way lube pressure abnormal. Lubrication system cannot build adequate delivery pressure.
corrective_actions: STOP MACHINE IMMEDIATELY - running without lube causes guideway damage
Check reservoir level first
Inspect pump motor operation
Check lube filter and replace if clogged

alarm_codes.description: Hydraulic pressure low. System hydraulic pressure below minimum for chuck and tailstock operation.
probable_causes: Chuck or tailstock cylinder seal leak
corrective_actions: Check hydraulic oil level and add ISO VG32 hydraulic oil
Check system pressure on gauge (should be 25-50 bar)
Inspect for external leaks at chuck and tailstock cylinders
Listen for pump cavitation

alarm_codes.description: Spindle drive fault. Spindle servo amplifier has detected an internal error.
probable_causes: Power supply voltage fluctuation during heavy cut
corrective_actions: Power cycle machine and check if alarm clears
Record alarm sub-code from diagnostic screen
Measure spindle motor insulation resistance (should be >1 MOhm)
Contact Okuma service with sub-code

maintenance_schedule.task: Check and refill way lube reservoir
procedure_steps: Visually inspect way lube reservoir level through sight glass on right side of machine
Level should be between LOW and HIGH marks
If low, add Okuma-approved ISO VG68 way lube oil through filler cap
Check for oil puddles under machine indicating line leaks

parts_needed.description: Way lube oil ISO VG68 (20L pail)

safety_warnings: Use only recommended lubricant grade — wrong viscosity causes premature guideway wear

maintenance_schedule.task: Check hydraulic oil level and chuck pressure
procedure_steps: Check hydraulic reservoir sight glass — level between MIN and MAX
Verify chuck pressure gauge reads 25-40 bar
Listen for abnormal hydraulic pump noise
Cycle chuck open/close twice and verify smooth operation
safety_warnings: Never operate with chuck pressure below 20 bar — risk of workpiece ejection

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean chip pan and check chip conveyor
procedure_steps: Remove chip tray and empty collected chips into chip bin
Clear any long stringy chips from around turret and tailstock
Inspect chip conveyor belt for damage or chip jamming
Run conveyor forward and reverse briefly to verify operation
Clean coolant tank strainer basket
safety_warnings: Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling metal chips
Ensure spindle is stopped and chuck is empty before reaching into work area

procedure_steps: Before first cut of the day, run warmup program
S200 for 5 min, S500 for 5 min, S1000 for 5 min, S2000 for 5 min, S3500 for 5 min
Monitor spindle bearing temperature on diagnostic screen
Temperature should stabilize within 5 deg C of ambient + 12 deg C
safety_warnings: Do not skip warmup — thermal shock causes bearing preload shifts and accuracy loss
Ensure chuck is empty during warmup

procedure_steps: Use refractometer to measure coolant concentration
Target range: 6-10% depending on material being cut
Measure pH with test strip or meter — target 8.5-9.5
If pH below 8.0, tramp oil contamination likely — skim and add fresh concentrate
Record readings in coolant log
safety_warnings: Wear nitrile gloves when handling metalworking fluid

maintenance_schedule.task: Clean and inspect electrical cabinet air filter
procedure_steps: Open electrical cabinet filter cover on rear of machine
Remove filter element and blow clean with shop air (from inside out)
Inspect filter for tears or holes — replace if damaged
Reinstall filter and verify cabinet fan is running
safety_warnings: Do not open cabinet interior panels — high voltage present

maintenance_schedule.task: Inspect chuck jaw condition and seating
procedure_steps: Remove workpiece and inspect soft jaw gripping surfaces for wear grooves
Check jaw serration engagement — jaws must be fully seated in master jaw slots
Verify jaw numbering matches master jaw station (1-2-3)
Torque jaw bolts to 45 Nm if soft jaws have been rebored recently
Measure jaw runout with dial indicator in chuck — should be < 0.02mm TIR after bore
safety_warnings: Ensure spindle is locked and power is at E-stop before jaw removal

procedure_steps: Chuck a test bar (minimum 200mm long, ground OD) in main spindle
Support with tailstock live center
Indicate OD at chuck end and tailstock end with dial indicator on turret
Difference should be < 0.01mm/200mm
If out of spec, adjust tailstock lateral alignment screws per manual
Recheck and document values in calibration log
safety_warnings: Tailstock adjustment screws are sensitive — turn in 1/8-turn increments only

procedure_steps: Index turret through all 12 stations using M23
At each station, verify turret curvic coupling seats fully (clamp confirm on diagnostic screen)
Time each index — should be within 0.3s of 2.5s specification
If any station is slow or fails to clamp, clean curvic coupling faces
Inspect curvic teeth for damage or chip contamination
safety_warnings: Keep hands clear of turret during indexing cycle

maintenance_schedule.task: Replace coolant tank filter and skim tramp oil
procedure_steps: Turn off coolant pump
Skim floating tramp oil from coolant surface with oil skimmer or absorbent pads
Remove and replace coolant filter cartridge (25-micron)
Check coolant concentration after filter change
Restart pump and verify flow
safety_warnings: Wear gloves when handling used coolant filters
Dispose tramp oil per local environmental regulations

maintenance_schedule.task: Bar feeder roller and channel inspection
procedure_steps: Open bar feeder channel cover
Inspect polyurethane guide rollers for wear flats or damage
Check that rollers spin freely on bearings
Clean channel of chips and bar remnants
Verify pusher finger is not bent or worn
Lubricate pusher rod with light machine oil

parts_needed.description: Bar feeder guide roller set (65mm capacity)

safety_warnings: Disconnect bar feeder power before working inside channel

procedure_steps: Mount dial indicator on turret face with probe touching a fixed surface
Jog each axis in positive direction and zero indicator
Reverse axis direction and record backlash reading
Compare to stored compensation value on parameter page
Adjust compensation if measured backlash deviates by > 2 um
Record values in machine calibration log
Power off spindle and engage E-stop
Remove jaw bolts (3x per jaw, typically M8 or M10)
Remove old soft jaws from master jaw T-slots
Install new soft jaws — ensure jaw number matches master jaw station
Torque jaw bolts to 45 Nm in star pattern
Bore soft jaws to workpiece diameter + 0.05mm allowance
Verify chuck runout with dial indicator < 0.02mm TIR after bore

parts_needed.description: Soft jaw blank set (10 inch chuck, 3-jaw)

safety_warnings: Always verify jaw clamping force with test piece before production
Do not exceed 4000 RPM with soft jaws — centrifugal force can reduce grip

procedure_steps: Power off machine and depressurize hydraulic system
Place drain pan under hydraulic tank
Open drain valve and drain all hydraulic oil
Remove and replace hydraulic filter element
Close drain valve and refill with ISO VG32 hydraulic oil to MAX mark
Power on and cycle hydraulic system to bleed air
Cycle chuck and tailstock multiple times to circulate fresh oil
safety_warnings: Depressurize system completely before opening any connections
Dispose of used oil per local regulations

procedure_steps: Warm up machine for minimum 2 hours before measurement
Mount test bar in chuck and support with tailstock
Measure X/Z linear positioning accuracy with laser interferometer per ISO 230-2
Measure spindle runout at nose and at 200mm extension
Check tailstock alignment to spindle axis
Update pitch error compensation table if deviations exceed 3 um/m
Generate calibration certificate and file in machine records
safety_warnings: Laser safety glasses required during measurement

parts_book.description: Main spindle bearing set (front + rear, angular contact)
Lithium backup battery CR2032 holder assembly
Bar feeder guide roller set (65mm capacity)

programming_tips.topic: G96 CSS with G50 Speed Clamp — Mandatory for Turning
programming_tips.code_example:
G50 S3500
G96 S200 M03
G00 X50. Z2.
G01 X0. F0.15
(At X0, RPM would be infinite without G50 clamp)
programming_tips.description: G96 Constant Surface Speed adjusts RPM inversely with diameter. Without G50 to set the max RPM limit, the spindle will accelerate uncontrollably as the tool approaches centerline (X0). ALWAYS program G50 before G96. The G50 S-value should be the maximum safe RPM for the workholding setup — typically 3000-3500 RPM for chuck work.
gotchas: Forgetting G50 before G96 is the most common cause of spindle overspeed alarms on lathes
G50 is modal and persists even after switching to G97 — cancel with G50 S4000 if needed
G96 calculates RPM from the X-axis diameter value, not actual tool tip position — verify tool offset direction

programming_tips.topic: G76 Threading Cycle — Compound Infeed Depth Calculation
programming_tips.code_example:
G97 S600 M03
G76 P030060 Q100 R0.05
G76 X23.026 Z-25. P1487 Q500 F2.0
(M20x2.0 external thread: minor dia 23.026mm, depth 1.487mm, first cut 0.5mm)
programming_tips.description: G76 P word encodes three parameters: passes (03), spring passes (00), and infeed angle (60 degrees). The thread depth P value (in the second G76 line) is in microns — 1487 = 1.487mm depth. First cut depth Q is also in microns. Thread depth = 0.6134 * pitch for 60-degree ISO metric threads. Infeed angle 60 = compound (reduces one-sided cutting force), 0 = radial (used for acme/trapezoidal).
gotchas: P value in second G76 line is MICRONS not millimeters — P1487 = 1.487mm
First cut Q500 = 0.5mm is typical for M20 — scale Q with thread pitch
Spring passes (middle digits of first P word) eliminate taper at thread exit
Always use G97 constant RPM for threading — G96 CSS will cause pitch errors

programming_tips.topic: G71 Roughing Cycle — OD vs ID Considerations
programming_tips.code_example:
G71 U2.0 R0.5
G71 P100 Q200 U0.3 W0.1 F0.3
N100 G00 X20.
G01 Z0.
X40. Z-5.
Z-30.
X50.
N200 Z-60.
(OD roughing: contour goes from small X to large X)
programming_tips.description: G71 automatic roughing takes multiple passes along Z parallel to the spindle axis. For OD roughing, the contour profile (N100-N200) must go from small diameter to large diameter. For ID roughing, the contour goes from large diameter to small. U word is the finish allowance on X (diameter), W is finish allowance on Z. The U value in the first G71 line is the depth of cut per pass (radius, not diameter).
gotchas: Depth of cut U in the FIRST G71 line is RADIUS value — U2.0 removes 4mm diameter per pass
Finish allowance U in the SECOND G71 line is DIAMETER value — U0.3 leaves 0.3mm total on diameter
For ID roughing, U finish allowance must be negative (U-0.3) to leave material on the bore wall
G70 finish cycle uses the same N-block range — verify contour is correct for both rough and finish

programming_tips.topic: Bar Feeding Synchronization for Lights-Out Running
programming_tips.code_example:
M05
M09
G28 U0. W0.
M11 (Chuck open)
M200 (Bar feed push to stop)
G04 P1000 (1 sec dwell for bar settle)
M10 (Chuck clamp)
G04 P500
M96 (Part count +1)
programming_tips.description: For unattended bar feeding, the sequence must be: retract to home, stop spindle, open chuck, signal bar feeder to push, dwell for bar settle, clamp chuck, then resume cutting. The bar must push against a positive stop (either the spindle face or a programmed Z-position with a turret-mounted stop). Always include G04 dwell after bar feed push to allow the bar to settle before clamping.
gotchas: M11 (chuck open) will alarm if spindle is still rotating — always M05 first
Bar feeder push pressure must match bar stock weight — heavy bars need higher pressure
Include M200 timeout check in macro — if bar feeder does not confirm push within 10 sec, alarm and stop
Remnant detection (BF0002) must trigger part-off of last piece and bar eject sequence

programming_tips.code_example:
M05
G28 U0. W0.
T0800 (Live drill in station 8)
M19 (Spindle orient / C-axis engage)
G97 S3000 M03 (Live tool spindle ON at 3000 RPM)
G00 X25. Z5.
G01 Z-15. F0.1
G00 Z5.
M05
M09
programming_tips.description: For cross-drilling and milling with live tooling on the LB3000 EX II MY, the main spindle must be oriented (M19) to engage the C-axis. The live tool spindle is a separate motor (6000 RPM max) in the turret. S-code and M03/M04 commands switch to controlling the live tool spindle when a live tool station is active. Cross-drilling uses X-axis feed, while face milling uses Z-axis feed with C-axis indexing.
gotchas: M19 must be called before engaging live tooling — otherwise the main spindle is still in rotation mode
S and M03/M04 commands automatically switch to live tool spindle when live station is selected
Maximum live tool RPM is 6000 — not the main spindle's 4000 RPM
Coolant through live tool requires M50 (separate from M08 flood coolant)

programming_tips.topic: Safe Start Block for Turning Programs
programming_tips.description: Every turning program should start with a safe start block that cancels all active modal states and establishes known conditions. G28 U0. W0. homes both axes via intermediate point. G40 cancels TNRC. G80 cancels any active canned cycle. G97 ensures constant RPM before G96 is engaged. G99 sets feed per revolution mode. This prevents crashes when a program is restarted mid-cycle.
gotchas: G28 U0. W0. uses incremental — machine rapids to current XZ then to home, so there is no collision risk from intermediate move
G50 must come BEFORE G96 — OSP processes blocks sequentially
Include G40 to cancel TNRC even if you think it is not active — modal state may persist from previous program
T0100 selects tool AND applies geometry offset — always call T-word with full 4 digits

programming_tips.topic: G92 vs G76 Threading — When to Use Each
programming_tips.code_example:
(G92 single-block method — operator controls each pass)
G97 S600
G92 X24.5 Z-25. F2.0
X24.0
X23.6
X23.2
X23.026
X23.026
(Two spring passes at final depth)

(G76 automatic method — CNC calculates all passes)
G76 P030060 Q100 R0.05
G76 X23.026 Z-25. P1487 Q500 F2.0
programming_tips.description: G92 is the simple threading cycle where the operator programs each pass depth manually. This gives maximum control and is preferred for: first-article threads, difficult materials, interrupted threads, and non-standard thread forms. G76 is the fully automatic cycle where the CNC calculates infeed per pass based on constant chip area — it is faster for production threading of standard ISO metric or UN threads.
gotchas: G92 does NOT use compound infeed — every pass is radial, resulting in more cutting force
G76 with 60-degree infeed angle reduces cutting force but leaves a slightly rougher thread root
Both require G97 — NEVER use G96 for threading
For multi-start threads, use G32 with specific start positions or G76 with phase shift

programming_tips.code_example:
M05 (Stop main spindle)
M11 (Open main chuck)
G00 W2. (Sub-spindle advance to grip)
M210 (Sub-spindle chuck clamp)
G04 P500 (Dwell for clamp confirm)
M10 (Verify main chuck open)
G00 W-2. (Sub-spindle retract with part)
M211 (Sub-spindle ON)
programming_tips.description: On dual-spindle LB3000 EX II models, parts transfer from main to sub-spindle for back-end operations. The sub-spindle advances along the Z2 axis, grips the part while the main chuck releases, then retracts. Synchronization of spindle speeds (M200/M201 on some models) enables pickup at RPM for short cycle times. The part transfer position must account for part-off tool width and part length.
gotchas: Sub-spindle chuck must be verified clamped (clamp confirm signal) before main chuck opens
Spindle sync (speed matching) requires both spindles to be the same RPM and direction before transfer
Part-off tool must cut fully through before transfer — partial cut leaves a pip that jams sub-chuck
Z-axis position accuracy during transfer directly affects back-end feature runout

programming_tips.code_example:
G42 G00 X50. Z2. (TNRC right compensation ON)
G01 Z0. F0.2
X30. Z-10. (Taper with TNRC)
Z-40.
G40 G00 X55. (TNRC cancel — must be on departure move)
programming_tips.description: TNRC (G41/G42) compensates for the tool nose radius during contouring. Without TNRC, the tool path follows the theoretical sharp point, leaving material on tapers and radii. G41 = left compensation (tool on left side of workpiece when viewed from tool to part), G42 = right compensation. The tool nose radius and imaginary tip direction (T1-T8) must be set in the offset page.
gotchas: TNRC must be activated on an approach move BEFORE the first cutting move — not on the cutting move itself
Cancel G40 must be on a departure move AWAY from the part — never cancel during a cutting move
Imaginary tool tip direction (T-number in offset page) must match actual insert orientation
TNRC does NOT work correctly inside G71/G72 canned cycles on OSP — it is applied automatically by the cycle

programming_tips.topic: Spindle Load Monitoring for Tool Wear Detection
programming_tips.code_example:
IF [VSPLD GT 90] GOTO 8000
(Continue cutting...)
N8000 G00 X100. Z50.
M01 (Spindle load exceeded 90% — check tool wear)
GOTO 1
programming_tips.description: VSPLD reads the current spindle load as a percentage of rated motor capacity. In turning, spindle load correlates strongly with flank wear — a 15-20% increase over baseline load indicates the insert needs indexing. Program macro checks at the start of each part to detect worn tools before they cause scrap. Sudden load drop to near 0% during cutting indicates tool breakage.
gotchas: Baseline load varies significantly with material, DOC, and feed — calibrate per operation
In CSS mode (G96), spindle load changes with diameter even at constant chip load
VSPLD includes acceleration loads during rapid direction changes
For bar feeding operations, include load check after each bar advance to detect bent bars

safety_limits.consequence_of_violation: Spindle motor thermal shutdown, potential workpiece ejection from chuck at high RPM

safety_limits.parameter: Maximum spindle speed with soft jaws
safety_limits.consequence_of_violation: Centrifugal force reduces jaw grip — workpiece may eject

safety_limits.parameter: Maximum workpiece weight in chuck (no tailstock)
safety_limits.consequence_of_violation: Bearing overload, spindle vibration, chuck bolt fatigue

safety_limits.parameter: Maximum workpiece weight with tailstock support
safety_limits.consequence_of_violation: Tailstock and bed overload, Z-axis servo errors
Insufficient clamping force — risk of workpiece ejection during heavy cuts
Bar cannot pass through spindle bore, jams in collet or chuck
Workpiece contacts way covers or turret at maximum X travel
Exceeding rated rapid causes following error alarms
Insufficient air for chuck confirm, air seals, and chip blow-off

safety_limits.parameter: Maximum L/D ratio without tailstock support
safety_limits.consequence_of_violation: Part deflection causes chatter, taper, and poor surface finish. Use tailstock for L/D > 4.
Bearing preload loss, reduced accuracy, potential bearing seizure
Thermal growth exceeds compensation range, accuracy degradation

coolant_types.type: Neat cutting oil (for threading and bar work)
